declaration.declared_before: any model score was computed on any pair in this cohort
declaration.question: Within one assay, with amino-acid composition identical by construction and the independent-site evolutionary profile score matched, does a model's native sequence likelihood rank the variant with the better measured phenotype above the worse one; and if it does not, can supervised readouts on the same pairs recover that direction?
declaration.why_it_matters: R1 reports that adding an evolutionary profile removes 77-86% of the likelihood increment. This cohort removes composition and the independent-site profile component by construction rather than by regression adjustment, so it measures what directional ability survives. E21 measures the native scoring rule; E22 separates a failure of the scoring rule from absence of extractable information.
declaration.relation_to_manuscript: The submitted draft states that this matched-variant test has not yet been performed. E21 attaches to Results 1 after the profile-overlap paragraph; E22 attaches to the supervised-readout paragraph in the same subsection.

cohort.source: ProteinGym substitution assays, single substitutions only, restricted to the retained R1 common support
cohort.pair_rule: Two single mutants of the same wild type in the same assay, carrying the same wild-type residue and the same mutant residue at two different positions. Both full-length sequences then have identical length and identical amino-acid composition, and differ only in which position is substituted. Composition, chemistry, substitution-matrix score and length are therefore matched exactly, not adjusted.
cohort.phenotype_target: measured DMS score, z-scored within assay, oriented so that higher is the better phenotype as the assay declares its direction

phenotype_gap_threshold.units: within-assay standard deviations of the z-scored DMS score
phenotype_gap_threshold.fixed: declared as a constant, not tuned on any data

cohort.profile_score: independent-site evolutionary log-odds s = log f(mutant | position) - log f(wild type | position) from the assay's own alignment, with the pseudocount and sequence-weighting convention recorded in the output artifact

profile_match_threshold.rule: absolute value fixed as the 20th percentile of |delta s| over development-cluster candidate pairs that already satisfy the phenotype-gap threshold, then applied unchanged to evaluation clusters

tiers.T_open: pair rule and phenotype gap only; validity tier
tiers.T_match: T_open and the profile match; primary tier

cohort.disjointness: each variant appears in at most one retained pair within a tier, by a seeded deterministic greedy rule that does not read any model score

development_evaluation_split.unit: wild-type family cluster at 50% identity, as used by R1
development_evaluation_split.rule: all thresholds and the greedy rule are fixed on development clusters; every reported number comes from evaluation clusters

endpoints.E21_primary: direction accuracy D_match: the fraction of T_match evaluation pairs where the native likelihood is higher for the better-phenotype member. Null value 0.5.
endpoints.E21_validity: direction accuracy D_open on T_open, and the cluster-paired contrast D_open - D_match, which is the share of apparent directional ability carried by the independent-site evolutionary component
endpoints.E21_construction_check: profile direction accuracy on both tiers; on T_match it is expected near 0.5 by construction and is a check on the matching, not a competitor

E22_readouts.R_like: native likelihood alone, identical to the E21 primary
E22_readouts.R_seqprof: the 444 sequence, mutation-identity, position and length descriptors plus the profile score
E22_readouts.R_repr: the primary frozen-state readout of the submitted Methods added on top of R_seqprof

E22_primary_contrasts: R_seqprof - R_like: whether supervision alone recovers direction that the native rule misses
R_repr - R_seqprof: whether the frozen representation carries direction beyond profile and sequence features
endpoints.E22_validity: the same fitted readouts must retain their established out-of-family predictive performance on unmatched variants; if they do not, the fold machinery is broken and the matched reading is void

inference.interval: pointwise 95% paired group-bootstrap percentile interval, matching the project default

practical_margin.justification: a scoring rule that resolves fewer than 55 of 100 pairs whose measured phenotypes differ by at least one assay standard deviation cannot order candidates usefully for design

inference.multiplicity: declared per arm and per tier, unadjusted across arms; the arm list is frozen below and the two E22 contrasts form one declared family per arm
inference.forbidden: no threshold, tier, pair, arm or endpoint may be revised after any evaluation-cluster model score is read

arms.pooling: the masked arm is reported separately and never pooled with the autoregressive arms
arms.scale_axis: the ProGen2 ladder is a declared capacity axis because functional constraint dilution predicts no gain in directional ability with capacity; it is not a causal scale intervention

mechanism_hypotheses.scoring_rule_deficit: R_repr clearly above 0.5 while R_like is a bounded negative: the direction is present in the representation and the native rule fails to expose it
mechanism_hypotheses.information_absent_at_this_budget: R_repr also inside the margin of 0.5: the direction is not extractable from the frozen representation at this label budget, which is what functional constraint dilution predicts
mechanism_hypotheses.not_distinguished_by_this_design: target mismatch versus compression loss during pretraining; that needs a matched training intervention and is out of scope here

declared_limitations: The ProteinGym export carries no measurement replicates or uncertainty, so a large phenotype gap is an observed gap and is not independently confirmed as a true gap.
This cohort has been studied before, so this is a pre-specified reanalysis and not new external validation.
An interval covering 0.5 is not equivalence, zero information or absence of a biological effect; a bounded negative excludes an effect only at the declared margin.
Matching the independent-site profile does not match all evolutionary information; an alignment-based profile is not an upper bound on all sequence statistics.
Family clusters are the resampling unit; split seeds and pair rows are not additional biological replicates.

amendment_01.declared_before: any direction accuracy was computed on either support
amendment_01.reason: The inventory established two facts the original declaration did not account for. First, the retained panel already carries per-variant native-likelihood values on a within-assay rank scale for all 33 models, together with stored out-of-family predictions for the profile_sequence, B and B_R readouts; a within-assay rank preserves the ordering of any two variants drawn from the same assay, which is the only quantity a direction test reads, so both E21 and E22 can be answered at full arm breadth without new scoring. Second, no ProteinGym alignments are on disk: the profile is a retained UniRef50 independent-site lookup whose per-variant score is already a column, so the profile match uses that column rather than a newly built alignment.

supports.S1_retained_panel: The retained R1 common support: 25,728 variants, 201 assays, 163 family clusters, all 33 panel arms and three fold seeds. Native-likelihood direction is read from the retained within-assay rank. No new scoring. Reported for arm breadth, including the full text and joint arms.
supports.S2_expanded: An expanded ProteinGym single-substitution cohort scored fresh on the local L20 GPUs for the nine arms declared above, sized to the pair count the endpoint needs rather than to the maximum available. Reported for sample size and for raw-nats magnitudes that a rank cannot carry.

amendment_01.pooling: The two supports are never pooled and every reported number names its support.
amendment_01.rank_scale_limit: On S1 only the direction of a within-assay pair is read. No magnitude, difference in nats, or effect size in likelihood units may be computed from the rank scale, and none is reported.
amendment_01.what_this_amendment_may_not_do: It fixes no threshold, adds no arm to S2, and changes no endpoint, margin or decision rule. It was written before any direction accuracy on either support was computed.

amendment_02.declared_before: any direction accuracy or likelihood magnitude was computed on either support
amendment_02.reason: S1 reads a within-assay rank and so cannot report how large a likelihood difference is. Fresh scoring on S2 recovers nats, which allows one further descriptive question that the rank scale forbids: whether the native rule is wrong confidently or only wrong marginally.

secondary_descriptive_endpoint_S2_only.name: direction accuracy stratified by likelihood-difference magnitude
secondary_descriptive_endpoint_S2_only.definition: Partition T_match evaluation pairs into declared quantile bins of |delta log-likelihood| in nats, then report direction accuracy with its cluster-bootstrap interval within each bin.
secondary_descriptive_endpoint_S2_only.bins: quintiles of |delta log-likelihood|, boundaries fixed on development clusters
secondary_descriptive_endpoint_S2_only.reading: A flat profile near 0.5 across bins means the magnitude of a likelihood difference carries no information about which variant is functionally better, so the native rule is not merely uncertain but confidently uninformative. An increasing profile would instead mean the rule is informative where it is decisive, and would weaken the paper's claim.
secondary_descriptive_endpoint_S2_only.status: descriptive and secondary; it carries no verdict, enters no multiplicity family, and cannot overturn the primary endpoint

amendment_02.what_this_amendment_may_not_do: It fixes no threshold, adds no arm, and changes no primary endpoint, margin or decision rule.

amendment_03.declared_before: any number from the three additions below was computed on any support
amendment_03.trigger: The declared construction check failed and the declaration required it be reported prominently. Profile direction accuracy on T_match is 0.5500 [0.4730, 0.6243] rather than near 0.5, because matching |delta profile score| constrains the magnitude of the profile difference and not its sign. A residual independent-site ordering therefore survives in T_match, and the protein arms' 0.58-0.64 cannot be read as entirely net of the profile.

addition_1_signed_balance.definition: A subset of T_match in which the profile's directional vote is balanced by construction: equal counts of pairs where the higher profile score belongs to the better-phenotype member and to the worse-phenotype member, selected by a seeded rule reading only the phenotype and the profile score and never a model score.
addition_1_signed_balance.effect: Profile direction accuracy on T_balanced is 0.5 up to integer parity, by construction rather than by estimation, so any arm above 0.5 there cannot be carrying the independent-site profile.
addition_1_signed_balance.reporting: T_match is retained and reported unchanged; T_balanced is reported beside it. Neither replaces the other.

addition_2_net_of_profile.endpoint: the cluster-paired contrast D_model - D_profile on the same pairs, on T_match and on T_balanced
addition_2_net_of_profile.reason: This is the quantity that answers whether a model orders a matched pair better than the residual profile does, and it was not derivable from what was already reported. It needs no new scoring.

addition_3_position_control.endpoint: direction accuracy of declared position-only rules on the same pairs, plus a tier additionally matched on relative position
addition_3_position_control.rules: (a) prefer the member whose substituted site is nearer a sequence terminus; (b) prefer the member whose site has the larger relative distance from the sequence midpoint. Both read only the position and the length, never the phenotype, the profile or a model.
addition_3_position_control.reason: The two members of a pair differ only in which site was substituted, so any systematic dependence of likelihood on position becomes a directional vote. Terminal regions are both more tolerant and differently contexted for an autoregressive model, so a position-only prior could reproduce an accuracy near 0.6 without any mechanistic knowledge. This control decides whether the surviving signal is mechanistic or positional, and it is the strongest alternative explanation of the retained E21 result.
addition_3_position_control.reading: If a position-only rule matches the protein arms' accuracy, the retained signal is a positional prior and must be described as one. If the arms exceed it, that margin is the defensible measure of non-positional directional ability.

power_statement_not_a_result.observation: At 190 matched pairs over 73 clusters the narrowest 95% interval across arms is 0.119 wide against a bounded-negative band 0.100 wide, so the bounded-negative verdict is arithmetically unreachable on S1 T_match. Every non-supported arm there is necessarily unresolved and none may be read as a bounded negative or as absence of an effect.
power_statement_not_a_result.requirement: Certifying the declared 0.05 margin needs roughly 400 to 500 matched pairs at this cluster structure.
power_statement_not_a_result.status: This is a statement about resolution, declared here so it cannot later be mistaken for a finding. The margin itself is not moved.

amendment_03.what_this_amendment_may_not_do: It moves no threshold already fixed, changes no primary endpoint, does not alter the 0.05 margin or the decision rule, and does not retract or restate any number already computed. The three additions are new readings on the same declared cohort.

amendment_04.declared_before: any number from the additions below was computed on any support
amendment_04.trigger: Both supports now agree that the two confounds are each individually beaten and never jointly controlled. On the open tier the arms exceed the position-only rule by a resolved +0.090 to +0.148, but the profile is uncontrolled there at 0.669. On the profile-balanced tier the profile is exactly 0.5 by construction, but the arms-minus-position margin resolves for zero of nine arms at 168 pairs. The quantity the paper's claim turns on -- directional ability that is neither site-wise conservation nor sequence position -- has therefore never been measured at adequate resolution. Also, the magnitude-matched position tier declared in amendment_03 failed its construction check on S1, putting the position rule at 0.418, below chance by more than the margin, so magnitude matching is the wrong instrument for position.

addition_1_sign_balanced_position.definition: A subset in which the position-only rule's directional vote is balanced exactly: equal counts of pairs where the site nearer a terminus belongs to the better-phenotype member and to the worse-phenotype member, selected by a seeded rule reading only position, length and phenotype. Position-neutral pairs are excluded rather than retained, so the balance is exact and not parity-dependent.
addition_1_sign_balanced_position.replaces: the magnitude-matched position tier of amendment_03, which is retained in the S1 artifact with status failed and is not to be built again

addition_2_double_balanced.definition: A subset of T_match in which the profile vote and the position vote are each balanced exactly by the same construction. The script must refuse unless both balances are exact.
addition_2_double_balanced.why_this_is_the_decisive_tier: An arm whose accuracy excludes 0.5 here has pairwise directional ability that is neither the independent-site evolutionary profile nor sequence position, measured by construction rather than by adjustment. This is the strongest form of the question the manuscript asks, and it is the one reading that can support or refute the central claim on its own.
addition_2_double_balanced.reading: Arms resolved above 0.5 establish non-positional, non-profile direction and its size. Arms whose interval lies inside the declared margin are a bounded negative at that margin. Arms with wider intervals are unresolved and must not be read as either.

addition_3_power.change: The per-cluster retention cap of 40 pairs is a sizing rule introduced during execution for variance control, not a declared threshold. It is retained for T_open, which already resolves every endpoint, and lifted for T_match, T_balanced, T_position_balanced and T_double_balanced, whose power is the binding constraint.
addition_3_power.target: at least 400 to 500 evaluation pairs in each balanced tier, which is the resolution the amendment_03 power statement names
addition_3_power.guard: Report the per-cluster pair-count distribution for every tier, so cluster dominance can be checked rather than assumed. The resampling unit stays the wild-type family cluster, so within-cluster counts affect a cluster's own precision and not the across-cluster inference.
addition_3_power.not_a_threshold_change: No phenotype gap, profile threshold, disjointness rule, dev/eval split, margin, decision rule or arm list is altered.

reporting_convention_to_unify.defect: The two supports reported the practical-size reading against different oracle definitions: one took the oracle's gain as half the mean pair gap, the other as the full mean pair gap, and separately reported a share of the chance-to-oracle interval in accuracy units. Three different quantities were called a share.
reporting_convention_to_unify.requirement: Report the accuracy-displacement share and the phenotype-gap-capture share as separately named quantities, each with its definition stated beside it, and state the oracle convention explicitly. Do not combine them into one number.

amendment_04.what_this_amendment_may_not_do: It moves no declared threshold, changes no primary endpoint, and does not alter the 0.05 margin, the decision rule or the arm list. It adds two sign-balanced tiers, lifts an execution-time sizing cap on the matched tiers, and fixes a reporting convention.
